# theory-B prior-art check (Q2), 2026-10-04 ~04:50Z — quotes with locations, verdicts, search list

Producer: theory-B leaf. Outside assessment: UNASSESSED. Verdicts are "known" or "not found in searched sources" ONLY; no worldwide-novelty claim.
Text extraction: arXiv HTML pages downloaded with curl and converted to text (LaTeX alttext kept); math rendered as $...$ in quotes below.

## Sources read (full text unless stated)
1. Gabric & Sawada, "Construction of orientable sequences in O(1)-amortized time per bit", arXiv:2401.14341 v4 (abs page: v1 25 Jan 2024, v2 17 May 2024, v3 24 May 2024, v4 10 Jul 2026), https://arxiv.org/html/2401.14341v4 (full HTML). Also v1 HTML.
2. Mitchell & Wild, "New orientable sequences", arXiv:2507.02526 (only v1, 3 Jul 2025, per abs page), https://arxiv.org/html/2507.02526 (full HTML). Published version (Acta Informatica 2026, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00236-026-00528-z): page did not load — UNREACHABLE.
3. Alhakim, Mitchell, Szmidt, Wild, "Orientable sequences over non-binary alphabets", arXiv:2407.14866 (Cryptogr. Commun. 16 (2024)), https://arxiv.org/html/2407.14866 (full HTML). [The task listed 2409.00672 under these four authors; 2409.00672 is actually Mitchell & Wild — both read.]
4. Mitchell & Wild, "Orientable and negative orientable sequences", arXiv:2409.00672 v5 (DAM 377 (2025)), full HTML.
5. Mitchell & Wild, "Special orientable sequences", arXiv:2411.17273 v1 (AJC 94 (2026)), full HTML.
6. Mitchell & Wild, "New upper bounds for the period of a negative orientable sequence", arXiv:2602.04433 v2 (6 Feb 2026), full HTML.
7. Mitchell & Wild, "Constructing orientable and negative orientable sequences with asymptotically optimal period", arXiv:2603.18646 v2 (14 Aug 2026), full HTML.
8. Mitchell & Wild, "Negative avoiding sequences", arXiv:2603.25286 v2 (23 Apr 2026): abstract only (k>=3 topic).
9. Mitchell & Wild, "Constructing orientable sequences", preprint dated 2nd January 2022, https://pure.royalholloway.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/44602256/Orientable_seqs_220102.pdf (text extracted by a crude PDF stream parser; quotes below are from that extraction).
10. debruijnsequence.org/db/orientable (fetched 2026-10-04).
11. Dai, Martin, Robshaw, Wild, "Orientable sequences", Cryptography and Coding III (OUP 1993) pp. 97-115: FULL TEXT UNREACHABLE (Royal Holloway portal https://pure.royalholloway.ac.uk/en/publications/orientable-sequences/ has metadata only, no PDF; no other copy found). U_n and its attribution are taken from sources 1 and 9, which agree.
Unreachable / blocked: OEIS (HTTP 403 / Cloudflare challenge), arXiv search and export API (HTTP "Rate exceeded" at ~04:42Z), Google Scholar (no tool). Web searches run (general engine): (a) Dai Martin Robshaw Wild "Orientable sequences" 1993 pdf; (b) "orientable sequence" upper bound period binary 2026; (c) "orientable sequences" maximum length exact values n=8 92 linear programming OR SAT; (d) "orientable sequences" "integer programming" OR "linear programming" OR "SAT solver" maximum period binary de Bruijn; (e) "maximum length" "orientable sequence" binary n=8 OR n=9 OR n=10 exact; (f) Alhakim Mitchell Szmidt Wild "Orientable sequences over non-binary alphabets" arXiv. Hits beyond the list above: Gabric-Sawada CPM 2024 (LIPIcs 296) and k-ary paper arXiv:2407.07029 (constructions; not read in full), arXiv:2510.16545 (random universal cycles; not relevant by title), ResearchGate copies.

## Exact quotes
Q-a (source 1, Section 1): "Orientable sequences do not exist for $n=1$ , and somewhat surprisingly, the maximum length $M_{n}$ of an $\mathcal{OS}(n)$ is known only for $1<n\leq 7$. Since the number of palindromes of length $n$ is $2^{\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor}$, a trivial upper bound on $M_{n}$ is $(2^{n}-2^{\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor})/2=2^{n-1}-2^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}$."  Abstract: "Maximal length orientable sequences are known only for $n\leq 7$".
Q-b (source 1, Section 2.1): "Their upper bound $U_{n}$ is the following: $U_{n}=2^{n-1}-\frac{41}{9}2^{\frac{n}{2}-1}+\frac{n}{3}+\frac{16}{9}$ if $n\bmod 4=0$; $2^{n-1}-\frac{31}{9}2^{\frac{n-1}{2}}+\frac{n}{3}+\frac{19}{9}$ if $n\bmod 4=1$; $2^{n-1}-\frac{41}{9}2^{\frac{n}{2}-1}+\frac{n}{6}+\frac{20}{9}$ if $n\bmod 4=2$; $2^{n-1}-\frac{31}{9}2^{\frac{n-1}{2}}+\frac{n}{6}+\frac{43}{18}$ if $n\bmod 4=3$." Footnote: "These bounds correspond to $\tilde{L}_{n}$ and $\tilde{U}_{n}$ , respectively, as they appear in [2]." Table 2 (n: L*_n / U_n): 8: 92/96; 9: 174/206; 10: 416/443; 11: 844/918; 12: 1844/1908; 13: 3700/3882; 14: 7694/7905; 15: 15394/15948; 16: 31483/32192; 17: 63135/64662; 18: 128639/129911; 19: 257272/260386; 20: 519160/521964.
Q-c (source 9, Sec. 2.2): "Theorem 2.5 (Dai et al. [8]) Suppose S is an OS(n) (n >= 5). Then the period of S is at most: [same four cases as Q-b]" ; "The values arising from Theorem 2.5 for 5 <= n <= 9 are given in Table 1. Observe that the bound of Theorem 2.5 does not appear to be sharp for n > 5; as noted in the introduction, Sawada (see http://debruijnsequence.org/db/orientable) has shown that the maximum periods of an OS(6) and OS(7) are 16 and 36 respectively." Table 1: 5 6, 6 17, 7 40, 8 96, 9 206.
Q-d (source 10): "The maximum length of an orientable sequence is known only for $n \leq 7$." and "a tighter bound $U_n$ is given in the table below [DMRW93]".
Q-e (source 2, Sec. 2.3): "Lemma 2.14. Suppose $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 2$ . Suppose $S$ is an $\mathcal{OS}_{k}(n)$ and consider a vertex in $B(S,n)$ with label $\mathbf{a}=(a_{0},a_{1},\ldots,a_{n-2})$ , where $\mathbf{a}$ is symmetric. Then $\mathbf{a}$ has even in-degree and even out-degree in $B(S,n)$ . Proof. Both $S$ and $S^{R}$ correspond to an Eulerian circuit in $B(S,n)$ , and these circuits are edge disjoint and cover all the edges of $B(S,n)$ . If $\mathbf{a}$ is symmetric then both circuits pass through this vertex equally many times." Also Lemma 2.7 (B(S,n) has 2m edges, in=out, subgraph of B*). Intro: "In this paper we first give new upper bounds on the period of an orientable sequence, which improve on the previous bounds for $n\geq 3$ ." Thm 2.22(iv), k=2: n even: $(2^{n}-3\cdot2^{n/2}+2^{2}-2)/2$; n odd: $(2^{n}-3\cdot 2^{(n+1)/2}+2^{3}+2^{2}-4)/2$; Table 1, k=2 column: n=5: 8 (11), n=6: 21 (27) [new (old)]. Abstract: "apart from very small cases a significant gap remains between the largest known period for such a sequence and the best known upper bound."
Q-f (source 3, Sec. 4): "Lemma 4.10 Suppose $n\geq 2$ , $r\geq 1$ , $S=(s_{i})$ is an $\mathcal{OS}_{q}(n)$ , and $\mathbf{v}=(v_{0},v_{1},\ldots,v_{n-r-1})$ is a $q$ -ary symmetric $(n-r)$ -tuple. Then $|L_{S}(\mathbf{v})|$ is even." ($L_S(v)$ = n-tuples with prefix v appearing in S or S^R.) "Observe that, although the theorem below applies in the case $q=2$ , the bound is much weaker than the bound of Dai et al. [ 9 ] which is specific to the binary case. ... The result can be seen as a generalisation of [ 9 ] , Theorem 2.2."
Q-g (source 6): abstract: "The approach used to develop the new bounds involves examining the nodes in the subgraph of the de Bruijn graph corresponding to a negative orientable sequence, and to consider the implications of the fact that the in-degree of every vertex in this subgraph must equal the out-degree." (Sec. 3.2 "Degree-parity constraints on the nega-sequence-subgraph"; k>=3 objects.)
Numeric hits for 426 / 7738 in sources 4 and 6 are table entries for q-ary (q>=3) negative orientable sequences (e.g. source 4 table row q=5 "... 1538 7738 ..."; row q=8 "... 62 426 3052 ..."), NOT binary M_n.

## Verdicts (per question)
1. Palindromic-node equality (root's cut x_{v0}=x_{1v}, x_{v1}=x_{0v}): its integer content is KNOWN. For binary, "v symmetric => even in/out-degree in B(S,n)" (Q-e, Mitchell-Wild 2025 Lemma 2.14; also the r=1 case of Alhakim et al. Lemma 4.10, Q-f, described there as generalising Dai et al. 1993 Theorem 2.2) is equivalent, given balance and reverse-freeness, to "both-or-none" at v, whose linearisation is exactly the root's equalities. The use of it as LP equalities inside a flow/LP relaxation: NOT FOUND in searched sources.
2. LP bound of this type (balanced reverse-free arc LP + palindromic equalities; Theorem 1's min-cost-routing value; any LP/IP/SAT bound): NOT FOUND in searched sources (the published binary upper bound remains Dai et al.'s U_n; MW 2025 Thm 2.22 is weaker than U_n for k=2 at every n=5..40, computed exactly in thm2_check.py).
3. Values M_8=92, M_9=194, M_10=426, M_12=1856 (and M_11=860, M_13=3728, M_14=7738) or any published upper bound at or below them: NOT FOUND in searched sources. Sources 1 (v4, July 2026) and 10 state maxima are known only for n<=7. Lower bound 92 is published (Table 2, L*_8 = 92); 194, 426, 860, 1856, 3728, 7738 exceed every published L*_n (174, 416, 844, 1844, 3700, 7694).
4. Parity cut for general reversal-closed vertex sets S (Lemma 3 of theory-B/theorem): singleton case KNOWN (Q-e); prefix-class variant KNOWN (Q-f, Alhakim et al. Lemma 4.10: tuples with a symmetric prefix v of length n-r) — a different family; the set-S family: NOT FOUND in searched sources.
5. Order of magnitude 2^{n-1} - M_n = Theta(n 2^{n/2}) (Theorem 2(g)): NOT FOUND in searched sources (the published upper bounds U_n, MW Thm 2.22 give deficit Theta(2^{n/2}) only).
6. Exact LP value / min-cost-routing characterisation (Theorem 1), explicit delta-potential bound (Theorem 2): NOT FOUND in searched sources. Note system2 child B (this pursuit, unpublished) reported the odd-n closed form and an "R=R'" statement without proofs.
Caveat: Dai et al. 1993 could not be read; their derivation of U_n (and their Theorem 2.2) may contain counting arguments related to Theorem 2; the comparison above is with their stated bound only.

## Claim-by-claim verdicts
| # | claim | outcome class | exact supporting check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | (root) Cut lemma: every 0/1 x with (P),(B) satisfies (C) at every palindromic (n-1)-node | reproduced (proof audited) + reproduced-null (no counterexample) | Hand proof: (vb)^R = b v, so the four arcs at palindromic v form reverse pairs {v0,0v},{v1,1v}; over {0,1}, a+b=c+d, a+c<=1, b+d<=1 forces (a,b,c,d) in {(0,0,0,0),(1,0,0,1),(0,1,1,0)}, i.e. a=d, b=c; for v=0^{n-1} (resp. 1^{n-1}) the palindromic arc counts 0 and the remaining pair is forced to 0. lemma.py: pairing structure verified n=3..16, local enumeration 3 feasible / 0 violating. exhaust.py: all 0/1 (P),(B) solutions n=3,4,5 and all OS cycles of every period n=3..7 (4788 at n=7): 0 violations. mipfals.py: n=5..10 every C row both signs, binary max violation 0 (HiGHS, corroboration only); LP max violation 1/2, so (C) is a genuine cut. The root's 4-case proof on page -instrument matches mine. |

LP(P,B only) = 10,22,44,101,202,439,878,1874,3748,7771,15542. |

Improves the LP bound 15508 by one. |
| 9 | "new-candidate" / field novelty of M_10..M_15 | unassessed | not my task; no novelty claimed. |

## Findings (first-class)
F1 (checker defect, confirmed, reproducer). Every check in check_cert.py — format, n/T range, label membership, y>=0, split validity and the decisive leaf test `assert b<T` — is a Python `assert`. With `python3 -O check_cert.py X` or `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1` all are removed and the program prints VERIFIED for any parseable certificate. Reproducer: take the n=10 certificate from -certificates-a, set "T": 400 -> default run: "AssertionError: leaf bound 426 not < T=400"; `python3 -O`: "VERIFIED ... => M_10 <= 399" (false; OS(10) of period 426 exists). Empty leaf {"y":{},"u":{}} -> under -O "VERIFIED ... max leaf bound=992". Remedy: explicit `if not cond: print('REJECTED ...'); sys.exit(1)` for every check, or abort at start `if not __debug__: sys.exit('refusing to run with -O')`. All root results were produced with default invocation (my independent checker agrees on every certificate), so no published bound is affected. scan_os.py has the same pattern (`assert set(s) <= {'0','1'}`), minor.
F2 (format, minor). certificates-b internal nodes include "lp" (see claim 6).
F3 (robustness, minor, sound). check_cert.py uses json.load: duplicate keys are resolved last-wins (y "P:0000100010": first "-50", last "3" -> VERIFIED; reversed order -> REJECTED), floats are accepted (exact via Fraction(float)), int() coerces T=427.0, unknown keys are ignored. The checked object is always a valid certificate, so this is not unsound, but certificate bytes can be read differently by another parser. My checker rejects duplicates, float literals, NaN, booleans and unknown keys.
F4 (observation). In the root n=14 tree the root split is redundant (its x0 subtree alone, without the split, verifies; swapping root children verifies). Harmless. My own n=14 tree needs only 3 leaves.

## Line audit of check_cert.py (beyond F1, F3)
- Model rebuilt from strings: W = non-palindromic words; P rows {a, a^R} keyed by lexmin; B rows out-minus-in with palindromic words dropped; C rows only for palindromic v with labels C:v:0/1, x_{vb} - x_{(1-b)v}. Matches the spec and my independent model (agreement on 22 certificates and 26/28 canaries; the 2 disagreements are F3 leniencies).
- Empty rows omitted from rowsE (none are empty for n>=3), so labels cannot alias; unknown labels rejected; P labels cannot be used in u and vice versa.
- Leaf bound: sum y + sum over w of (fixed1: r_w, fixed0: 0, free: max(0,r_w)) with r_w = 1 - (A^T mult)_w, exact Fractions; requires bound < T; for integer T and integral sum x this gives sum x <= T-1. Correct weak duality on the box.
- Tree: split must be a non-palindromic word not already fixed; both children required (KeyError otherwise); recursion covers x_w=0 and x_w=1, so leaf boxes partition {0,1}^W. A string/list node containing "split" crashes (TypeError), never accepts.
- No soundness gap found other than F1.

## Failed approaches / negative results
- Plain most-fractional branching and K=10 strong branching (score = max child LP only) stalled at n=11: the 862 LP face is massively degenerate (both children stay at 862 for >20 levels). Fixed by scoring (max child LP, child sum) over all fractional candidates.
- First primal rationalisation for n=15 with denominators <=64 failed (147 violated rows); denominators <=1000 succeeded.
- n=15 with T=15507 (target M_15 <= 15506): stopped-unverified. My B&B (K=60) reached depth >=5 after ~30 min with one child stuck at LP 15507 at every level (degenerate face); no certificate. A second n=15 T=15508 run with K=20 was stopped once the K=60 run finished.
- Could not falsify the cut lemma: exhaustive (n<=7), MIP (n<=10) and witness tests (n=8..14) all null.

## Open next step
- Root: harden check_cert.py against -O (F1) and decide whether "lp" is part of the format (F2); re-publish the checker hash.
- n=15: find an OS(15) witness (lower bound) and/or push the B&B to T=15507; the persistent 15507 child suggests either an integral (P),(B),(C) point of size 15507 exists (possibly disconnected) or a deeper tree/stronger cuts are needed.

## Termination
Phase 1 and Phase 2 complete; extra n=15 exploration recorded. Settled voluntarily before the 07:05Z limit.

## Failed approaches (details: failed page)
No closed form for D_n; uncapacitated distance and f(delta) potentials do not reach D_n; heuristic separation stalls (replaced by exact T-odd-cut separation); prefix family alone insufficient for n=13,15,16; explicit-dual certificates too large; v2/v3 checkers unsound under python3 -O (fixed by v4); n=18 parity closure stuck at 128796; n=20 parity loop (63 rounds, ~560 cuts): no decrease below LP 519285 (stopped).
